rows.row_extraction: csv_table_rows: read_csv(BytesIO(raw)) -> df.to_dict('records'); not a JSON row array. Daily path requests outputsize=full CSV; intraday path fans the same /query path out over one URL per %Y-%m month in the date range and concatenates each month's CSV records; symbols split on ',' and gathered via asyncio.gather
rows.notes: Response is CSV, not the keyed-JSON form: TIME_SERIES_*(&function=&outputsize=full&datatype=csv) returns a flat timestamp/open/high/low/close table, so no year/quarter keying here. interval picks function via INTERVALS_DICT and MONTHLY/WEEKLY are rewritten to DAILY then resampled client-side (W-FRI/M agg first/max/min/last/sum); adjusted results are recomputed via calculate_adjusted_prices and renamed (timestamp->date, 'adjusted close'->adj_close, split_coefficient->split_factor); transform_data filters start_date<=date<=end_date client-side; intraday splits_only is downgraded to splits_and_dividends with a warning. UNMAPPED_SUGGESTION: client_side_ohlcv_resample — no existing key covers re-aggregating daily bars into weekly/monthly OHLCV with per-column agg rules plus split/dividend adjustment recomputation; derived_columns only names column arithmetic, not period resampling.

rows.row_extraction: nested_key: rows live under annualEarnings or quarterlyEarnings (chosen by period param) as a flat array of period dicts (fiscalDateEnding/reportedEPS/estimatedEPS/surprisePercentage/reportedDate) — the year/quarter labels are fields inside each dict, not object keys; each item is stamped with symbol taken from the request URL query and truncated to limit before extend; one URL per comma-separated symbol via amake_requests callback
rows.notes: function=EARNINGS, one JSON doc per symbol; no pagination. target='annualEarnings' if period=='annual' else 'quarterlyEarnings' (line 124). validate_null maps string 'None' and '0' to None for eps/surprise (line 73); normalize_percent divides surprise_percent by 100 (line 83); empty results raise EmptyDataError after collecting 'Information' rate-limit messages. metric_branch is the closest existing key for the annual/quarter branch but the branch selects a response JSON key, not an endpoint or metric feed. UNMAPPED_SUGGESTION: response_key_branch — existing keys cover endpoint/metric branching, not picking which nested array of the same response to explode.
